expert_proposals.title: Reverse cost-model direction: lower random_page_cost 1.5->1.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->0.6
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: GetUserTweets consumes 87.6% of terminal capacity at p50=138us with a single Index Scan plan; the r011 upward cost-model move (random_page_cost 1.5->3.0, seq_page_cost 0.8->1.0) was refuted on TPS and inconclusive on latency, so the cost-model direction is unresolved and must be retried with a larger safe amplitude in the opposite direction.
expert_proposals.mechanism: GetUserTweets is a single-row Index Scan (estimated_rows=1, cost 8.45) whose per-call latency dominates terminal time. With the working set fully cached (2TB RAM, shared_buffers 512MB, effective_cache_size 8GB), random reads are effectively as cheap as sequential, so the incumbent random_page_cost=1.5 over-prices index paths relative to seq_page_cost=0.8. r011 raised both costs and was refuted; the paired decision was inconclusive, not refutation of the direction. Lowering random_page_cost to 1.0 and seq_page_cost to 0.6 keeps the ratio cache-consistent and lets the planner prefer the cheapest index path for the skewed user_id predicate, reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call and freeing terminal capacity.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets remains on an Index Scan but with a cache-consistent cost model that should not penalize the index path; no plan regression expected since estimated_rows=1 already selects Index Scan.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small positive: freeing GetUserTweets terminal capacity by even 1-2% translates to ~300-600 rps at 32.4k baseline.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease modestly (1-2%); other transaction types unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from incumbent 1.5 to safe low bound 1.0 (allowed [1.0,6.0]); reverses the refuted r011 upward direction (1.5->3.0) with a larger safe amplitude downward, consistent with fully-cached working set.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: planner cost of random/cached reads; lowering it favors index paths for the dominant GetUserTweets transaction

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Lower from incumbent 0.8 to 0.6 (allowed [0.5,2.0]); paired with random_page_cost to keep the ratio cache-consistent and reverse the refuted r011 upward move (0.8->1.0).
knob_changes.mechanism_role: I/O cost scale paired with random_page_cost; lowering it keeps the cost model consistent with cached reads

predictions.rationale: Cache-consistent lower random_page_cost should not change the Index Scan choice but reduces estimated cost pressure, keeping the cheapest path; p50 should not regress and may improve slightly.
Same mechanism; p95 tail should follow p50 if the index path is retained without cost-model-induced plan churn.
Freeing terminal capacity on the dominant transaction class raises completed transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: If the cost-model change does not alter the GetUserTweets plan (already Index Scan), latency and TPS will be unchanged within noise, indicating the cost model is not the binding constraint and the bottleneck is elsewhere (e.g., WAL commit path).

If WAL commit-path queueing (wal_waiting_backends, sync_average_ms) is the true binding constraint, cost-model changes will not move GetUserTweets latency and TPS will be flat; the WAL bundle should then be revisited.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: r011 tested the upward direction (random_page_cost 1.5->3.0) and was refuted on TPS; the paired decision was inconclusive, so the direction is unresolved. This proposal retries the same cost-model mechanism with a larger safe amplitude in the opposite (downward) direction, consistent with the fully-cached working set.

nodes.label: Cache-consistent cost model keeps GetUserTweets on cheapest Index Scan path

expert_proposals.title: WAL commit-path bundle: widen group-commit window and writer flush batch
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: commit_delay=100us with commit_siblings=2 opens a fixed per-commit sleep that rarely collects siblings at 5 terminals, while wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer-side flush batching; WAL sync average 0.111ms and wal_waiting_backends p95=1 persist.
expert_proposals.mechanism: The incumbent pays a fixed 100us commit_delay on every commit but commit_siblings=2 means the window activates almost always, adding latency without reliably coalescing fsyncs; wal_writer_flush_after=0 forces the WAL writer to flush per write. Widening commit_delay to 200us with commit_siblings=3 makes the window activate only when >=3 backends are committing, so the sleep is amortized over a real group, and setting wal_writer_flush_after=64 (512kB) lets the writer batch background WAL writes. Together these reduce per-commit fsync frequency and WAL queueing, freeing terminal capacity for GetUserTweets.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets is read-dominated and unaffected directly; reduced commit-path queueing lowers InsertTweet latency and frees terminal capacity shared with GetUserTweets.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small increase (>=0.3%) if WAL sync coalescing reduces commit stalls; neutral if WAL is not the binding constraint.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: InsertTweet p95 decreases; GetUserTweets p50/p95 unchanged.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Widen from 100us to 200us within safe [0,1000]; paired with commit_siblings=3 the window activates only for real groups, amortizing the sleep.
Raise from 2 to 3 within safe [0,20]; with 5 terminals, 3 siblings gates the window to genuine concurrent commits instead of nearly every commit.
Set from 0 to 64 (8kB units = 512kB) within safe [0,1024]; enables writer-side flush batching so background WAL writes coalesce instead of flushing per write.

predictions.rationale: Larger writer flush batch and a group-commit window that only activates with >=3 siblings coalesce fsyncs, lowering average sync time.
Fewer per-commit fsyncs reduce backends waiting on WAL.
Reduced commit-path queueing frees terminal capacity, raising completed transaction TPS.

alternatives.statement: WAL sync is already fast (0.111ms) and not the binding constraint; the bundle yields no measurable TPS change and sync_average_ms stays within noise.
Widening commit_delay to 200us adds latency without collecting siblings, so InsertTweet p95 rises and TPS falls.

expert_proposals.why_exceeds_incumbent: Incumbent commit_delay=100/commit_siblings=2 activates the sleep on nearly every commit without reliably grouping, and wal_writer_flush_after=0 disables writer batching. Raising commit_siblings to 3 gates the window to real groups and enabling a 512kB writer flush batch coalesces background WAL writes, targeting the persistent wal_wait anomaly.

nodes.label: Group-commit window gated to real sibling groups plus writer-side flush batching coalesce fsyncs

expert_proposals.title: Restore default SIRead granularity to cut predicate-lock bookkeeping
expert_proposals.configuration_cause: Incumbent forces coarsest SIRead granularity (max_pred_locks_per_page=0, max_pred_locks_per_relation=0), which promotes every page/relation predicate to relation-level SIRead locks; with 5 terminals and 3.5M GetUserTweets calls this inflates lock bookkeeping (locks_total p95 340, max 460) without any lock waits (lock_waiting_backends max 0).
expert_proposals.mechanism: The incumbent sits at the coarsest SIRead extreme (page=0, relation=0). Coarser granularity means each scanned page promotes to a relation-level SIRead lock, so per-transaction lock bookkeeping grows with the number of relations touched rather than being capped per page. Restoring PostgreSQL defaults (page=2, relation=-2) keeps page-level SIRead locks up to 2 per page and lets relation-level promotion follow the default fraction of the per-txn budget, reducing lock churn per GetUserTweets while leaving the generous 8192 per-txn budget intact. Since lock_waiting_backends is already 0, the win is bookkeeping/CPU, not wait removal.
expert_proposals.query_effect: GetUserTweets (87.6% of terminal capacity) should see slightly lower per-call lock bookkeeping; no plan change expected.
expert_proposals.expected_tps_effect: Small positive: reduced lock bookkeeping frees CPU on the dominant transaction class; magnitude bounded because lock waits are already zero.
expert_proposals.expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p99 flat-to-slightly-down; no regression expected on other classes.

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default 2, inside allowed [0,256]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default midpoint.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: page-level predicate-lock granularity cap; 2 keeps up to 2 SIRead locks per page before promotion instead of promoting every page

knob_changes.numerical_basis: PostgreSQL default -2, inside allowed [-2,4096]; reverses incumbent 0 extreme toward default fraction of per-txn budget.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: relation-level predicate-lock granularity cap; -2 uses the default fraction of the per-txn SIRead budget instead of forcing relation-level promotion

predictions.rationale: Default page/relation caps stop every page from promoting to relation-level SIRead locks, lowering total lock count p95.
Less per-call lock bookkeeping trims the dominant transaction's tail.
Freed CPU on the 87.6%-capacity transaction class raises completed-transaction goodput.
No lock waits exist today; granularity change must not introduce them.

alternatives.statement: If the residual bottleneck is WAL commit-path queueing rather than lock bookkeeping, restoring SIRead defaults will leave locks_total.p95 and GetUserTweets p99 unchanged while wal_waiting_backends.p95 stays at 1.
If promotion churn is budget-bound rather than granularity-bound, the default caps will not reduce locks_total.p95 and only a larger max_pred_locks_per_transaction would.

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage owns the WAL commit-path bundle; wal_waiting_backends.p95=1 persists and is not addressed here

unverified interaction note (demoted to pending constraint): wal_writer_flush_after
